answer: Admission uses a bandwidth lease rather than a reusable bond. Every identity must reserve a 2 Mbps relay for 16 epochs and publish one unpredictable 64 MB transcript per epoch. A funding-cluster mesa raises the kth lease to 2k Mbps, so 100 aliases reserve 10,100 Mbps. Each transcript includes the prior checkpoint anchor and a sampled canyon path; validators fetch random chunks, reject reuse, and bar the whole cluster for 32 epochs after two failed samples.
